simulationIndexing.title: Simulations in the knowledge base
simulationIndexing.auto: Index every simulation when it finishes
simulationIndexing.autoDesc: Adds to the project’s knowledge base a summary of the run, its statistics, the elements outside their thresholds and what changed since the previous run. This is what lets you ask the chat what problems the last simulation found.
simulationIndexing.raw: Also index the full time series
simulationIndexing.rawDesc: Additionally stores the raw results, step by step. It does not improve the chat’s answers —that is what the summaries are for— and takes up far more space; it is meant for fine-tuning stages.
simulationIndexing.thresholdsDesc: The regulatory reference varies by country. The defaults are the values in common use: pressure between 14 and 70 m —in rural water systems the minimum drops to 7— and a maximum velocity of 3 m/s.
simulationIndexing.inherited: Inherited from the general settings; they part ways as soon as you change something here.
simulationIndexing.ownSettings: This project has its own settings.

networkView.expertReview: requires review by a water-supply expert before it is used in real decisions.
networkView.todiniHint: Todini index, network entropy and hydraulic redundancy. Compares before/after the outage scenario simulated above.
networkView.residualPressure: Residual pressure: {{presion}} m · {{horas}} h out of service
networkView.baselineAffected: Without the event the network was already leaving {{afectados}} people without service, out of {{total}}.
networkView.excludedNodes: Excluded {{count}} junction(s) with negative base demand (sources modelled as demand junctions):
networkView.notConverged: The simulation did not converge at every step. The figures for those steps are not reliable.
networkView.outageIntro: Simulates the failure of one or more components (pipe, pump, valve) and estimates the impact on service, in pressures and in people without water. A single run in PDA mode (pressure-dependent demand) returns both results.
networkView.hazardSourceHelp: Where does the intensity come from? Seismic codes in Latin America and the Caribbean rarely give PGV. If you only have PGA, use the PGA input with the soil class of the site.
networkView.componentsHelp: Median in g at 50 % probability. There is no default: no published table we can cite covers these components, so they are left to whoever knows the region. Left blank, the curve is not drawn.
networkView.coefWhere: To find coefficients for your region, see annexes 5A and 5B of
networkView.userCoefficients: Coefficients supplied by the user, not published by Boorie.
networkView.methodBase: Lognormal repair-rate fragility from {{modelo}}, with generic per-material parameters — requires validation by a water-supply expert before being used for real decisions.
networkView.methodPga: PGA input: the median of {{medianaPgv}} cm/s becomes {{medianaPga}} g via Newmark & Hall (1982), α = {{alfa}} cm/s per g for {{suelo}} soil. The PGV–PGA correlation is only moderate (ρ≈0.70–0.73, Bradley 2012), so the PGA curve carries that uncertainty; with measured PGV, use PGV.

descargo.parrafoModelos: Boorie is a decision-support tool, not a substitute for professional judgement. Calculation, simulation and analysis results come from models with assumptions and from the data you provide. Their validity depends on the network being described correctly and on the model being applicable to the case; Boorie can check neither.
descargo.parrafoIA: Answers generated by artificial intelligence may be inaccurate or incomplete, even when they look confident. Check them before acting on them.
descargo.parrafoDecision: No decision about real infrastructure should be made from a Boorie figure without validation by a qualified professional and, where regulation requires it, by a professional licensed to sign the project.
descargo.parrafoResponsabilidad: You are responsible for the use you make of the results and for complying with the regulations that apply to you.
descargo.avisoCorto: Model output: requires professional validation before being used for real decisions.
descargo.avisoIA: AI-generated answer: it may be inaccurate. Check it before acting on it.
descargo.avisoExportado: Generated by Boorie. Decision-support tool: requires validation by a qualified professional before being used for real decisions.
descargo.prevalece: The Spanish version is the one that prevails; English and Catalan are courtesy translations.

**The request took too long.** It could not be completed within the time limit (8 minutes).

Possible causes:
- The AI model is overloaded or too large
- The knowledge search (RAG) is taking a long time
- Connection problems with the AI provider

What you can try:
1. Send the message again
2. Use a smaller or faster model
3. Turn the Wisdom Center off for a moment if you have it on
